title: I love flowers Id love to have the whole place swimming in roses
html_source: Molly’s rose-filled house is a symbol for the domestic pleasure that she and Bloom seek throughout this chapter. It creates a new meaning for the family name “Bloom,” which depicts the act of blooming and flourishing, which is also given by the usage of flowers. Molly is again connected with natural beauty and transformation. She responds to Stephen and Bloom’s philosophical, scientific, and religious problems in her own unique way: through action. She doesn’t wait for the ideal circumstances, the universe to make sense, or fate to unveil itself. Instead, she makes use of the tools at her disposal to create something beautiful out of nothing.
